title: P@x provider configuration
description: How P@x reaches one model provider: which provider, which model, the output limit, timeouts, retry behaviour, and optionally prices and a limit for one task. The API key is never part of this file: it lives in the system keyring. The loader in services/tur-pax-providers is authoritative. It also enforces rules this schema cannot express: a base URL may use plain http only for a loopback host, retry.initial_delay_ms may not exceed retry.max_delay_ms, task_limit.max_cost needs prices, the openai-chat family needs a base_url, and send_back_reasoning is accepted for openai-chat only.

duration_ms.description: A duration in milliseconds, at most one hour.

price.description: A price per million tokens, in the currency of the prices.

provider.description: The adapter family, which selects the adapter. anthropic: the Messages API. openai: the Responses API. google: the Gemini Interactions API. openai-chat: the OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions API that DeepSeek, other services and local model servers offer; it has no public address of its own.

base_url.description: The base URL of the provider's API, without the path of an endpoint. Without it the family's public endpoint is used; openai-chat has none and needs one, given as the service documents it, up to the path /chat/completions (for example https://api.deepseek.com, http://127.0.0.1:11434/v1). Set it to use a compatible gateway. It must be https://host[:port][/path]; http is accepted for a loopback host only. User information, a query and a fragment are not accepted.

send_back_reasoning.description: openai-chat only. Whether the reasoning text a service streams beside the answer (reasoning_content, reasoning) is sent back with the assistant turns of later requests. Set it only for a service whose documentation requires it: DeepSeek, when tools are offered. Otherwise the reasoning is kept with the conversation and never sent.

model.description: The model name, as the provider spells it. There is no default: model names are configuration and are never compiled in (ADR-0004).

max_output_tokens.description: The most output tokens the model may produce for one request. There is no default.

connect_ms.description: The longest wait for the connection to be established.

response_ms.description: The longest wait for the provider to start answering.

idle_ms.description: The longest silence tolerated in the middle of a stream.

retry.description: How failed requests are retried. Only failures the providers document as transient are retried: a rate limit, an overloaded or unavailable service, a connection that could not be made and a timeout. A rejected request is never retried, and nothing is retried once any of the response has been delivered.

max_attempts.description: The most times one request is sent, the first attempt included.

initial_delay_ms.description: The delay before the second attempt. It doubles for each later attempt. Used when the provider names no delay.

max_delay_ms.description: The longest delay between two attempts. If the provider asks for a longer delay, the request is not retried and the delay is reported.

prices.description: Prices per million tokens, for showing what a task cost. There are no default prices. Without this object only tokens are counted.

currency.description: The currency the prices are in, for display.

input_per_million.description: The price of a million input tokens.

output_per_million.description: The price of a million output tokens, the model's reasoning included.

cached_input_per_million.description: The price of a million input tokens read from the provider's cache. Without it they are priced as ordinary input.

task_limit.description: The limit for one task. A stream is stopped when the task goes over it. At least one of the two limits must be set.

max_cost.description: The most a task may cost, in the currency of the prices. Needs prices.

max_tokens.description: The most tokens a task may use, input and output together.
